clue.text: Trainee with problem knocked back wine

indicators.note: knocked back means the word for a problem is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a cadet is a trainee officer

explanation.surface: A trainee, troubled by something, drinks a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like downing a drink, but it is the reversal signal, and 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscadet is a dry white variety from the Loire valley in France.

clue.text: Tenfold increase for head of General Assembly

indicators.note: in Roman numerals the first letter, worth 100, is multiplied by ten to become the one worth 1000

parts.note: George Custer was an American general

explanation.surface: A general assembly votes for a tenfold rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General Assembly' reads as one body; the general is CUSTER, whose C (100) becomes M (1000).
explanation.definitionFit: A muster is a gathering of troops for inspection, an assembly.

clue.text: Parched, stopped by pub for a round

indicators.note: stopped by means plugged by, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: sere means dry or parched
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: Thirsty, someone calls in at the pub to buy a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a round' looks like drinks but means a ball shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a perfectly round solid, a ball or globe.

clue.text: Judge computing speed after a run

indicators.note: after says the speed term comes behind the first two letters

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
bit rate is the speed of data transfer in computing

explanation.surface: An official assesses how fast a computer runs.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to settle a dispute as an impartial referee, so to judge it.

clue.text: They don't like Brussels sprouts — ice cream's top hit around Spain

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround a single letter
hit means damaged or knocked about, so these letters are scrambled
top picks the first letter of the word cream

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Brussels sprouts and a frozen dessert are struck around a Spanish table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brussels sprouts' reads as vegetables: Brussels, seat of the EU, ends the definition, and sprouts starts the anagram fodder that 'hit' scrambles and 'around' wraps round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Opponents of the European Union, whose institutions sit in the Belgian capital.

clue.text: Perhaps border strike creates chaos

parts.note: a flower bed is one kind of garden border, hence 'perhaps'
to lam is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A violent clash at a frontier causes disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, named after a London asylum, is a synonym for uproar and confusion.

clue.text: Cream cake at last that's low-calorie

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word cake

parts.note: lite is a marketing spelling for reduced-calorie food

explanation.surface: A cream cake that is finally lower in calories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream cake' looks like one item; Cream is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, the select group.

clue.text: Seducer reluctant to have a port

parts.note: loth means unwilling or reluctant
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A womaniser is unwilling to drink a glass of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink but is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, a character in a Rowe play, became a byword for a rakish womaniser.

clue.text: Fail to put straight what forgetful actor may do? Sounds like it

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is spoken the same as the phrase described

parts.note: a forgetful actor might skip a line of the script

explanation.surface: An actor who forgets lines fails to deliver them right.
explanation.definitionFit: To misalign is to set something out of true, so not to arrange it straight.

clue.text: Bruch set out to be a composer

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Max Bruch arranged something to become another composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bruch is himself a composer, which makes him look like the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Schubert is an Austrian example of the classical writer of music.

clue.text: Success by American boxing amateur offers a break

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one letter is held inside the others

parts.note: a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A winning American fighting a non-professional gives a pause in the bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like sport but puts A inside HITUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a gap or pause in continuity, a synonym for an interruption.

clue.text: Apprehended officer's heard — by this?

indicators.note: heard means the phrase is spoken, giving the same sound as the answer

parts.note: apprehended means caught, and a marshal is a senior officer; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: An arrested officer's case is tried before a military tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' does double duty: a case is heard by a tribunal, and the spoken phrase gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A military court tries members of the armed forces, so a detained officer would face it.

clue.text: Bird nested in winter, generally going west

indicators.note: going west says the hidden letters are read backwards
nested in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, fitting for a bird

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bird spends winter in a nest, usually heading westward.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Bird nested' as the definition; 'nested in' is the containment signal, so the definition is just 'Bird'. In an across clue 'going west' means right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron, an example of a wading bird.

clue.text: Hold up progress, defending one wicket?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, batting purely defensively; the question mark admits the cryptic reading of a single wall of stone

explanation.surface: A batsman blocks progress by stubbornly protecting a single wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicket is the set of stumps a batter defends; the second reading also pictures one stone wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall or obstruct is the general sense; cricket uses the verb for dogged, scoreless defensive batting.

clue.text: P. Morgan pined, desperately trying to appear well-connected

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Piers Morgan longed hard to look like he knew important people.
explanation.walkthrough: Piers Morgan is a British TV presenter, which makes the surface pointed.
explanation.definitionFit: Casually mentioning famous acquaintances is the habit of someone wanting to seem socially connected.

clue.text: Praise God for one song not starting

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
eg, for example, means for one

indicators.note: not starting removes the first letter of the word for a song

parts.note: a lyric is a song or its words

explanation.surface: Worshippers praise God, for example with a song that never quite begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A panegyric is a formal speech or text of high praise, an encomium.

clue.text: Sounds like you cracked up, put in a higher position

indicators.note: sounds like says only the spoken form of the word is used

parts.note: the letter U is spoken the same as the pronoun
to be cracked up is to be praised highly

explanation.surface: It seems you broke down laughing while being raised up.
explanation.definitionFit: Upraised means lifted or elevated, raised up.

clue.text: Support spot check

parts.note: a rest is a support, as in an armrest
a spot of rain is a light shower, so it can stand for rain

explanation.surface: An inspection to confirm something is properly supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot check' reads as a random inspection; spot is the rain, check the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or curb, so to check.

clue.text: Religious people bearing grudge with tense foreboding

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: PI is short for pious, a crossword stand-in for religious
to resent is to grudge
men are people
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Devout people harbouring resentment feel an anxious sense of doom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious people' looks like one unit; Religious gives PI, which carries RESENT, and people gives MEN. 'with' joins T.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentiment is an intuitive feeling that something bad is about to happen, a synonym for foreboding.

clue.text: Writer goes around street to find restaurant

indicators.note: goes around means encircles, so the street letters go inside the pen

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, something that writes

explanation.surface: An author tours the neighbourhood looking for somewhere to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like an author but is a Biro, a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant.

clue.text: Fail to justify fellow's trust

parts.note: to belie a promise is to fail to fulfil or justify it

explanation.surface: Someone fails to warrant a friend's confidence in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief is confidence or faith in something, a synonym for trust.

clue.text: I craft, i.e. intricately? Right

indicators.note: intricately suggests a complicated reworking, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A skilled maker describes their work as detailed and agrees it is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a skilled worker could say 'I craft intricately', and 'Right' agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled craftsman or inventor, someone who makes things with skill.

clue.text: Lecturer tucked into square meal

indicators.note: tucked into means put inside, so the letter goes within the number

parts.note: four is a square number, two times two

explanation.surface: An academic eats a hearty, full dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' and 'square meal' suggest eating; meal is ground grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Meal is coarsely ground grain, so finely milled wheat is a kind of it.

clue.text: Beef is good and ready to eat

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to be eaten

explanation.surface: The meat is fine and cooked enough to serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' looks like meat but is the slang verb or noun for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a complaint or grumble.

clue.text: Commercial breaks present gloom

indicators.note: breaks means splits open, so one word is cut apart by another

parts.note: to show is to present
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: Advertising interruptions spoil a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial breaks' reads as TV adverts, but 'breaks' is the containment signal splitting the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadow means darkness or partial darkness, a synonym for dimness.

clue.text: Texts of operas Britten mostly composed after 51

indicators.note: after says the Roman number stands in front of the rearranged name

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are arranged anew
mostly means all but the last letter of the composer's name is used

explanation.surface: Benjamin Britten wrote most of his opera words after turning fifty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Britten was an English opera composer, so 'composed' reads as writing music.
explanation.definitionFit: Libretti is the plural of libretto, the words of an opera.

clue.text: They give fellow sailor stocking filler finally

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

indicators.note: stocking means filling, so the sailor's letters hold another

parts.note: OS is ordinary seaman

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word filler

explanation.surface: A man and a seaman supply something to put in a Christmas stocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking filler' looks like a Christmas present, but 'stocking' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Donors are people who donate, so they are those who give.

clue.text: Strike gets half of department to stop work

parts.note: to clock someone is to hit them
the first half of department is depart, which means go off

explanation.surface: Industrial action gets half the office staff to down tools.
explanation.walkthrough: The half is taken twice over: 'department' halves to DEPART, and to depart is to go OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to record leaving and finish the working day.
